lead.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia's chief executive after 33 years
lead.dek: Finance chief Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis; shares closed down 4.3% and House chairs gave Huang until Friday evening to agree to testify
body: Nvidia's board said Thursday that Jensen Huang, 63, the co-founder who has run the chipmaker since 1993, resigned as president, chief executive and director effective immediately, four days after he told employees he had an affair with a former executive of a Singapore data-center firm whom U.S. intelligence agencies believe was a Chinese asset, an allegation Beijing denies.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress becomes interim chief executive while keeping her post, and Harvey C. Jones becomes the board's first independent chair. Shares fell as much as 14.3% at the open and closed down 4.3% at $166.19; CBS News put the market value erased since last week's close at almost $500 billion, and the stock was 27% off its record through Wednesday.

The chairs of the House China, Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees gave Huang until Friday evening to accept a Dec. 1 closed-door interview or face a subpoena, and Senate Banking chair Tim Scott wants him and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick before his panel in December. Independent directors have retained former acting U.S. Attorney Joon H. Kim to investigate; quarterly results are due Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Brooklyn collapse toll rises to 8, including 2 children, as search ends
briefs.summary: FDNY ended rescue operations Thursday afternoon at the Flatbush Avenue site after drones and canine units found no more victims; 17 people were hurt. The Brooklyn district attorney is investigating, and the city is inspecting about 100 related construction sites.

briefs.headline: Van Hollen challenges Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
briefs.summary: The Maryland senator, 67, announced Thursday the first open challenge to Chuck Schumer, 75, with Bernie Sanders' endorsement; Schumer said he has the votes. Democrats will hold 55 seats in January with Alaska still uncalled, and leadership elections are expected in early December.

briefs.headline: USDA proposes rule that would drop 6.3 million people from SNAP
briefs.summary: The rule published Tuesday would end automatic eligibility for people receiving other aid in 41 states and D.C.; the department estimates 6.3 million people, 1.8 million of them children, would lose benefits by fiscal 2029. Enrollment was 36 million in July, down 13% in a year.

briefs.headline: ICE deportations reached a record 483,200 in fiscal 2026, DHS data show
briefs.summary: Removals rose from 442,640 the year before and were about 78% above fiscal 2024, with more than 491,000 arrests, according to Homeland Security figures obtained by CBS News. The network's analysis found more than half of July's arrests involved people with no convictions or pending charges.

briefs.headline: Putin and U.S. envoys agree to resume direct talks; Kushner says Europe joins next round
briefs.summary: After about two hours with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow Thursday, the Kremlin called the talks useful and said bilateral negotiations resume after nine months. The envoys then met Zelensky near Dublin; Kushner said Europeans join the next round, which Moscow did not confirm.

briefs.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they struck a U.S. radar site in Bahrain
briefs.summary: The IRGC said Friday it targeted an early-warning radar in retaliation for a Thursday air attack on a telecommunications tower in Hormozgan province; neither Washington nor Manama had commented. Bahrain hosts the U.S. Fifth Fleet, and it is Iran's first claimed strike on U.S. assets in a Gulf state since early September.

briefs.headline: Trump says he would 'certainly consider' military force against Cuba
briefs.summary: In a radio interview with Hugh Hewitt on Thursday, the president said he wants the situation resolved before he leaves office in 2029, the first time he has put a timeline on it. The U.S. has run an oil blockade of the island since January and issued an arrest warrant for Raul Castro.

briefs.headline: Haitian police retake the national stadium from gangs after two years
briefs.summary: National police and the government's private task force took back Sylvio Cator Stadium in Port-au-Prince on Thursday, and Salvadoran troops from the roughly 2,000 Nayib Bukele sent took over its security. Gang control had forced Haiti to play World Cup qualifiers in Curacao.

briefs.headline: Appalachian Power pledges $17B for gas plants and $7.5B to keep coal units to 2050
briefs.summary: Gov. Patrick Morrisey said Thursday at a Charleston energy summit that the utility will build three gas-fired plants adding 3 gigawatts by 2031 and extend its coal plants' lives; his office said the investments will not raise rates. Coal producers used the summit to ask for a cut in the 5% met-coal severance tax.

briefs.headline: Hanshaw says the House is 'primed to act' on the $410M school formula, carefully
briefs.summary: A day after the Department of Education priced its rewrite, the speaker called for a methodical, multi-year review of cost drivers, especially special education, and warned against consolidation as a universal answer. Enrollment is down 8,270 students in a year and 8 to 20 schools face closure.

briefs.headline: Barboursville School to reopen as a 36-bed treatment facility for foster children
briefs.summary: The state signed a five-year lease with Youth Health Associates to reopen the psychiatric facility that closed in 2025, Morrisey said Thursday in Cabell County; it opens in early 2027 with 50 to 60 jobs. West Virginia had 5,719 children in foster care July 1, its lowest July count since 2016.

briefs.headline: PSC approves $17.3M Mountaineer Gas rate increase; $5.35 more a month from Dec. 1
briefs.summary: The settlement, approved in an Oct. 28 order, raises base-rate revenue 9.75%, down from the $26.8M requested in February, and lifts the average residential bill 5.82%. It stacks on the $2.38 monthly infrastructure charge that takes effect Jan. 1; the company agreed to no new base-rate case before Feb. 1, 2028.

regional.item: Cabell County commissioners certified the Nov. 3 results Thursday: 22,791 of 56,482 registered voters cast ballots, and Rep. Carol Miller lost the county by 56 votes.
A Kanawha judge removed Prosecutor Debra Rusnak's office Thursday from the case of the former EMT charged with dragging a man two miles behind an ambulance.
Discovery World children's museum broke ground Thursday on an expansion backed by a $750,000 United Bank gift, with the building due to be ready for a traveling exhibit in May.

away.item: Police were called to the village polling place on Election Day, Nov. 3, after a poll watcher challenged college students' right to vote; the state says up to six voters were affected.

hotspots.item: Republican Sam Hall of Cowen, who unseated the incumbent in May's primary, won the contested Webster County Commission seat over Democrat Robin Cutlip on Nov. 3.
Pender school board members toured Topsail Middle in Hampstead Thursday night to size up a ninth-grade campus for Topsail High, estimated near $50M; a vote is set Monday.

briefs.headline: SD57's new board reverses the 28% trustee pay raise its predecessor voted in May
briefs.summary: Trustees voted Tuesday to undo increases that would have taken the chair from $30,460 to $39,000, on a motion from Shar McCrory citing the policy tying pay to the exempt-staff grid; pay instead rises 2.5%. Erica McLean cast the only vote against.

briefs.headline: Fatalities in a boating incident on the swollen Squamish River as a storm surge nears
briefs.summary: RCMP said several people were involved Thursday and some reached safety; Squamish SAR and North Shore Rescue deployed. Environment Canada issued a coastal flooding statement for Friday from Boundary Bay to the Gulf Islands, and more rain is forecast Saturday night into Sunday.

briefs.headline: Doerkson asks the outgoing NDP to stop tunnel-only spending on the Massey crossing
briefs.summary: The premier-designate wrote Thursday asking that transition work on the $8.5B Fraser River Tunnel Project be limited to what also supports a bridge, saying a bridge saves $2.5B; a June report put spending to date at $580.7M. His government is sworn in Nov. 20.

briefs.headline: Ottawa declares Stellantis in default and gives it 30 days before suing over Brampton
briefs.summary: After a Toronto meeting Thursday failed to reverse the plant's sale to Roshel, Industry Minister Melanie Joly ended the resolution process and said Canada will seek hundreds of millions of dollars; Stellantis offered to repay $24M. About 2,200 workers are on layoff benefits.

briefs.headline: Euclid's first big data release catalogs more than a billion objects
briefs.summary: ESA published 13 months of observations Wednesday covering about 1,900 square degrees, 14% of the planned survey, with more than 900 million galaxies and spectra for 160 million sources. The full first release, with weak-lensing data, is due in mid-2027.

briefs.headline: LHCb finds matter-antimatter asymmetry in Bs decays matches the Standard Model
briefs.summary: The first measurement of the time-integrated CP asymmetry in Bs to Ds pi decays, using 2016-2018 LHC data, found a difference of about one or two per thousand decays, within uncertainty, and rules out an unknown process above about 2%, in Physical Review Letters.

briefs.headline: Brain-flushing fluid waves during sleep weaken with age, MIT finds
briefs.summary: Comparing adults 18 to 39 with those 60 to 84 in two-hour sleep sessions, the Lewis lab found the cerebrospinal fluid waves that clear waste were significantly weaker in older sleepers, tracking weaker slow waves and reduced blood flow rather than less sleep, in Nature Aging.

briefs.headline: Robotic system keeps deep-sea microbes at seafloor pressure from seabed to lab
briefs.summary: Manchester's DISCUSS system recovered 34 isolates from a cold seep at 1,300 meters, including a bacterium that cannot grow at surface pressure, and sustained a community for 180 days, in Nature Sensors; fewer than 1% of deep-sea microbes can be cultured conventionally.

briefs.headline: OpenAI's own data show frontier models growing harder to monitor by their reasoning
briefs.summary: Tracking models from GPT-5 to GPT-6 Astra, the company found better pretraining and one architecture sharply increase silent multi-step reasoning and that distillation passes it on; Astra solves 31-minute human math problems with visible reasoning switched off, per a UK AISI figure.

briefs.headline: Four nonprofits sue Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceX to freeze new models
briefs.summary: Public Citizen, Heat Initiative, the Alliance for Secure AI and the Irreplaceable Education Fund filed in San Francisco Superior Court Thursday under California's unfair competition law, seeking an injunction on next-generation models; none of the companies had responded.

briefs.headline: United Airlines bars unauthorized AI agents from its booking channels
briefs.summary: The airline said third-party agents cannot complete bag declarations and other required steps and expose customer credentials, following U.S. and U.K. banks and Amazon in blocking Meta's Muse agent from acting on customers' behalf.
